stem: Make $r$ the subject of the formula $V = {=a}r^2h$. Which one of the following gives every value of $r$ that satisfies the formula?
solution: Start with $V = {=a}r^2h$. Divide both sides by ${=a}h$ so that $r^2$ stands on its own: $r^2 = \dfrac{V}{{=a}h}$.
Take the square root of both sides. A square has a positive and a negative root, so write both signs: $r = \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{V}{{=a}h}}$.
The root sign covers the whole fraction, so the answer is $r = \pm\sqrt{\dfrac{V}{{=a}h}}$.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Stops at the squared variable
proposed_misconceptions.description: After dividing to isolate r squared, the student writes the quotient as if it were r and never takes the square root.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Roots only the numerator
proposed_misconceptions.description: The student takes the square root of the top of the fraction only and leaves the denominator outside the root sign.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Multiplies instead of dividing
proposed_misconceptions.description: To undo the coefficient multiplying the squared variable, the student multiplies both sides by it instead of dividing.

notes: Basic entry point, modelled on book Ex 4.5 Q5 (V = pi r^2 h) with the constant pi replaced by a whole number so the options stay plain. It is an mcq on purpose: the answer is a symbolic expression carrying a plus-or-minus sign, and every distractor is a named slip of this objective (positive root only, no root taken, root of the numerator only, multiply instead of divide). The stem carries the hole a, so instances differ by stem and distinct_by_choices is not needed. Options are not equivalent for any a from 2 to 15.
